findings.description: The only test for the `Write or Edit then 0` arm sends an Edit payload with an invented `content` field. Write is the tool whose real response carries the whole file in `content`, so dropping `$tool == "Write"` would fail no test, and every Write over 20k would then get a false warning. Use a `tool_name: "Write"` payload.

The case "echo tsc is still a test log by design, but 5k stays silent" uses 5000 characters, which is under both thresholds, so it passes whether or not `echo tsc` is classified as a log. To pin the classification, use 10001-20000 characters and expect `warns`.

No test checks that the regex's `[^|;&\n]*` stops at a command boundary. The `pnpm test 2>&1` case has its `&` after `test`, so replacing the class with `.*` fails nothing. Add a negative case such as `pnpm install && cat test.txt` at 15k, expecting `silent`.

Only `tool_name == "Bash"` gets the stdout+stderr count and the 10k log threshold. A background `pnpm test` read back through TaskOutput has no `content`/`filenames` and counts as 0, and one read through Read gets the 20k plain threshold. Long backgrounded test runs are never warned at the log threshold.

The log-command regex hard-codes `pnpm test|typecheck|build`, a second copy of `TEST_CMD`/`TYPECHECK_CMD` in `.claude/project.env`, which other hooks read through `lib/project-env.sh`. If those commands change, the 10k threshold silently stops applying, and the tests still pass because they hard-code the same strings.

`2>/dev/null` plus `exit 0` swallows every jq failure, including a syntax error in the program or a missing `jq`, so a broken hook looks like a quiet one. Nothing catches that: `tool-result-size.test.sh` is wired into no `pnpm` script, lint step or CI workflow.
The Bash `isImage == true then 0` arm is a defensive branch with no test. Under AGENTS.md §Altitude it should get a test that names the real case, or be dropped.

No test exercises the generic `($r | type) == "object"` arm (`content` array via `text`, plus `filenames`), the `else` arm, WebFetch `result`, or a Read under the threshold. That leaves the most intricate jq paths uncovered.

The file-tree annotation `PostToolUse(Failure)` reads as a matcher on PostToolUse, because every other line uses `Event(matcher)`. The hook is actually wired on two events, so write it as `PostToolUse + PostToolUseFailure`, as the table row below does.

The row says "Edit and Write echoes and images count as 0", but only Bash `isImage` output is zeroed; an image returned by Read or an MCP tool is still counted. Write "Edit and Write echoes and Bash image output count as 0".

In the header, the clause "and failing test, typecheck and build runs are exactly what this is for" is motivational and adds no WHY beyond the payload-shape note before it. Drop it to tighten the comment.

process_issues.description: The PR's restored config copies were at `.claude-pr/.claude/<path>`, not the `.claude-pr/<path>` the briefs named first. The security and maintainability reviewers missed that fallback and read the PR's files from `gh pr diff 230` instead. The diff shows both new files in full, so coverage was not lost.
